items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: In fact the first band I was with was a guy named Bob Astor’s band

ctx.x: Can you recall at what age did you think you could actually make a career as a musician?

I recall every day of my life just about, I swear, all of it. Really. I remember asking my mother a question once, where I said, “Mom, you remember when you were scrubbing the floor in the kitchen?” And she uttered some obscenity about some neighbors or somebody, and I said, “were you talking about me?” She said, “no, honey, not you, no, no, I mean them.” So I said, “how old was I then?” She says, “you were two years old.” And after that she says, “I thought you were going to be a school teacher because I used to…

had a kid on trumpet named Neal Hefti, who was writing arrangements for the band, and Bob would say every Monday he had to bring in an arrangement for Tuesday rehearsal see, or Monday rehearsal, whatever. And during the week he’d say “Neal, how are you doing with the arrangement?” Neal would say “you’ll have it in time, don’t worry.” Came Monday for the rehearsal, he never got to the rhythm section. He wouldn’t finish the arrangement, because he couldn’t write a score.
